NDT training in Indianapolis: how it works for Indianapolis employers and technicians

NDT training for Indianapolis is delivered by Atlantis NDT as ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET — live online for technicians anywhere in Indiana, or onsite at your plant or shop under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer then certifies you under its written practice after training, documented experience, a Level III-administered exam set and a vision test.

Central Indiana is a manufacturing economy. NDT work here comes mostly from making things: aircraft engines and engine parts, transmissions and powertrains, diesel engines, steel, vehicles, pharmaceutical process equipment, and the supplier plants that feed them. Around that core sit steady in-service jobs such as boilers, pressure vessels and piping in utilities and process plants, highway bridges, rail yards, pipelines and airport maintenance.

That mix produces a two-track labour market. Aerospace suppliers usually work under an aerospace personnel standard flowed down by their customer. Industrial, utility and fabrication employers usually work under SNT-TC-1A with ASME and AWS codes. Technicians who understand both, and employers who keep their written practices straight between the two, have an easier time. Employers need technicians trained to their written practice and examined by a Level III. Individual technicians need training records and exam preparation that make them hireable. Atlantis has no training building in Indianapolis. Training is live online or onsite at your facility. Request an Indianapolis training quote. You will get cohort and onsite quotes within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Indianapolis

Each course follows the SNT-TC-1A recommended structure for its method and level. It covers principles, equipment, calibration, technique, interpretation and codes, with supervised practical work.

MethodLevelsWhat Indianapolis employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, IIIWeld inspection on pressure vessels and power piping, bond and thickness checks on manufactured parts, forging and bar inspection, bridge and structural weldsNone for Level I; Level II needs Level I plus documented experience per your written practice
Phased Array UT (PAUT)I, IIEncoded weld inspection in fabrication and construction, production inspection of components, corrosion mapping in process and power plantsNormally UT Level II first
Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD)I, IIFlaw sizing in heavy-wall vessel and structural welds, often paired with PAUTNormally UT Level II first
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, IIICastings and weld radiography in manufacturing, digital radiography on production lines, pipeline and power-piping weld radiographyNone for Level I training; NRC and state radiation rules apply separately
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, IIICrankshafts, gears, shafts and forgings in powertrain manufacturing; structural steel to AWS D1.1; bridge welds to AWS D1.5; rail and lifting equipmentNone for Level I
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, IIIFluorescent penetrant inspection of aerospace engine parts, stainless process equipment in pharmaceutical plants, non-magnetic castingsNone for Level I
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, IIIWeld and workmanship inspection in fabrication and assembly, bridge inspection support, and the visual element of every methodNone for Level I
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, IIISurface crack detection on engine and airframe parts, heat-exchanger tubing in utilities and process plants, bar and tube testing in metals productionNone for Level I

Level III preparation for engineers and senior technicians who will write procedures and certify staff. See ASNT Level III training. Indiana has many plants where the NDT function sits inside a quality department, so a Level III who understands production quality systems is especially useful.

A note on aerospace work. Engine and airframe suppliers in Indianapolis often work to NAS 410 or a customer-specific standard, and many require Nadcap accreditation. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based. It builds the method competence those schemes also test, but we do not issue NAS 410 certification. Check your contract. Ask a Level III which scheme your work needs.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Indianapolis, step by step

  1. Employer written practice. This sets training, experience, exams, vision and recertification rules for each method and level. It is the governing document.
  2. Formal classroom training. Delivered live online or onsite, with records per technician. Recommended minimums are in the training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. Method and total NDT experience, logged under certified supervision, often on production inspection or plant maintenance.
  4. General, specific and practical exams. A Level III administers all three. Specific exams test the employer’s procedures and specifications. Practical exams use real parts or specimens.
  5. Vision exam. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, recorded, usually every year. This matters in fluorescent PT and MT.
  6. Employer certification. The certifying authority signs the record for each method and level.
  7. Recertification. Renewal on the interval the written practice sets.

Employers can find more in SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Indianapolis crews

  • Live online. Instructor-led theory for technicians in Indianapolis, Carmel, Fishers, Greenwood, Anderson, Columbus, Lafayette, Kokomo, Muncie and Terre Haute, and statewide to Fort Wayne, Evansville and the Calumet region. Shift workers can take sessions scheduled around first, second or third shift. Documented attendance supports training records where your written practice allows it.
  • Onsite at your plant. Classroom and practical blocks at your facility, on your equipment, parts and reference standards, under ASNT Level III oversight. For manufacturers, training on the actual parts and acceptance criteria your inspectors use every day is the main advantage.
  • Blended. Online theory followed by a short onsite practical and exam block.

The practical exam is hands-on on real specimens and cannot be done online. We schedule around production schedules, model-year changeovers, summer plant shutdowns and utility outage seasons. Ask about onsite training for your Indianapolis crew, or see live online NDT training and corporate programmes.

Where NDT technicians work in Indianapolis

  • Aerospace engines and MRO. Indianapolis has one of the largest aircraft-engine manufacturing and engineering sites in the US, plus a network of suppliers making engine parts. The city’s airport hosts a major cargo hub, and regional airline maintenance is based in the metro area. PT, ET, UT and RT on engine and airframe parts are core methods.
  • Powertrain and heavy vehicles. Transmission manufacturing in Indianapolis and diesel engine manufacturing in Columbus anchor a large powertrain supply chain. MT on shafts, gears and forgings, UT on castings and bonded parts, and ET for surface and heat-treat checks are routine.
  • Automotive assembly. Vehicle plants around the state, in Lafayette, Princeton, Greensburg, Fort Wayne and Kokomo, and their tier suppliers generate weld and part inspection plus plant maintenance work.
  • Steel and metals. Steel mills near Crawfordsville and the integrated steelmaking complex on Lake Michigan in northwest Indiana need UT, MT, ET and VT on products, cranes, vessels and structures.
  • Refining and energy. The large refinery at Whiting in northwest Indiana, gas-fired and coal-fired power stations, and pipelines across the state run in-service inspection to ASME and API codes. They generate outage-season demand for UT, PAUT, RT and ET technicians.
  • Pharmaceutical and life sciences. Pharma manufacturing in Indianapolis uses stainless process equipment and piping, often to ASME BPE, where PT, VT and borescope inspection of sanitary welds are common.
  • Motorsport engineering. Speedway and the west side of Indianapolis host a motorsport engineering cluster. Crack detection by MT and PT on suspension, driveline and chassis parts is a niche but real source of work.
  • Bridges, rail and infrastructure. Highway bridges are inspected to AWS D1.5 and Indiana Department of Transportation requirements. Rail yards and lines through the Indianapolis hub need MT and UT on rolling stock and structures.

Radiography licensing in Indiana. Indiana is not an NRC Agreement State, although the state has formally signalled its intent to pursue an agreement with the NRC, so check the current status. Today the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission directly licenses radioactive material used for industrial radiography in Indiana, and 10 CFR Part 34 applies. Radiographers must be certified by an NRC-recognised certifying entity, such as ASNT’s Industrial Radiography Radiation Safety Personnel (IRRSP) programme. The state has jurisdiction over X-ray equipment, which matters for the many Indiana plants that use cabinet or production X-ray systems. All of this is separate from your SNT-TC-1A RT method certification.

What Indianapolis employers typically ask for: method certification to their written practice, the ability to work shifts, familiarity with quality systems such as IATF 16949 in automotive or AS9100 in aerospace, and for aerospace work, qualification under the customer’s personnel standard. Those are employer requirements beyond NDT training, but they decide who gets hired.

Level III services and written practices for Indianapolis NDT companies

Indiana has hundreds of plants where NDT is one function inside a larger quality department. When a customer audit or registrar visit arrives, the NDT programme is often where findings land. The written practice may be out of date. There may be no named Level III. Practical exams may not be documented against real parts. Vision records may have lapsed. Or procedures may not match current customer specifications.

  • Written practice development: a written practice built or revised for your methods, levels and customer flow-downs, kept separate from any aerospace-scheme document if you run both.
  • Level III services: procedure writing and approval, exam administration and grading, certification record review, and periodic oversight. See SNT-TC-1A guidance.
  • Audit preparation: a pre-audit gap review before customer, registrar or accreditation visits.
  • Onboarding: re-certifying newly hired technicians under your own written practice.

Book a Level III consultation for your Indianapolis programme.

Practise before the practical exam

Practical NDT, the Atlantis 3D simulator, lets trainees practise 12 methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. Indianapolis candidates heading into aerospace work can use the aircraft hangar and NDT lab scenes. Those heading into fabrication and plant work can use the welding workshop and storage tank scenes. The simulator is practice only. It does not replace the practical exam on real specimens and does not count as experience. For theory, use mock exams such as the UT Level II practice questions.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He oversees course content, examinations and Level III services for Indiana employers. See the full training catalogue.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Indianapolis

How do I get NDT certified in Indianapolis?

Complete formal training in your method and level, build documented experience under certified supervision, and pass the general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III. Pass a vision exam, and your employer certifies you under its written practice.

Can I take NDT training online in Indiana?

Yes. Theory is delivered live online, so technicians anywhere in Indiana can attend, including around shift schedules. The practical exam is hands-on, usually onsite at the employer’s facility under Level III oversight. See how online training works.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the training hours your written practice sets and on the documented experience you must build. See the training requirements matrix. Experience usually takes longer than the classroom.

Do I need a license for radiography in Indiana?

If you handle radioactive sources, yes. Indiana is currently not an Agreement State, so the NRC’s 10 CFR Part 34 applies, and radiographers need certification from an NRC-recognised body such as ASNT’s IRRSP. X-ray equipment is regulated by the state. Check current status, as Indiana has signalled intent to become an Agreement State. This is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification.

What does NDT training cost in Indianapolis?

Pricing is quote on request. It depends on method, level, group size, delivery format and any Level III services. We return cohort and onsite quotes within one business day. Request an Indianapolis training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Indianapolis employers?

SNT-TC-1A is widely used by industrial, utility, fabrication and manufacturing employers in Indiana. Aerospace suppliers often work to NAS 410 or customer standards instead of, or as well as, SNT-TC-1A. Check your employer’s requirements.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Indianapolis?

It depends on the sector. Aerospace suppliers lean on PT and ET. Powertrain and steel plants lean on MT and UT. Utilities and refining need UT, PAUT, RT and ET during outages. Fabricators and bridge work lean on VT, MT and UT.

Can you train our team onsite in Indianapolis, Columbus or Lafayette?

Yes. Onsite delivery on your equipment and parts, under ASNT Level III oversight, is the standard model for employer groups. We schedule around shifts and shutdowns.

Do automotive plants need NDT technicians?

Yes, though often inside quality or maintenance teams rather than as stand-alone NDT roles. Weld, casting and forging inspection and plant equipment maintenance all use NDT methods.

Can I get certified without an employer?

You can train and hold training records independently. SNT-TC-1A certification, though, is issued by an employer under its written practice.

Does Atlantis offer NAS 410, CWI or ISO 9712 training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. Those are separate schemes that some Indiana employers also ask for.

Is the simulator a substitute for hands-on training?

No. Practical NDT is for rehearsal only. Hands-on training and the practical exam use real equipment and specimens.
